sources.description: Released dataset of Preoţiuc-Pietro et al. (2016): 491 users' unigram and word2vec-cluster features. Used offline by scripts/derive-darktriad-scaling.py; not fetched.
The authors' instructions for applying the released Dark Triad word models.

transformations: CSV category labels mapped to historical public names; intercept and named structural features separated from lexical terms.
Spanish PERMA is DLATK's dd_sperma_v2 table, parsed (not executed) from its MySQL dump; it supersedes WWBP's earlier spanish_perma_v1.csv and the corrupted legacy JSON.

Big Five weights are the historical package's copy of WWBP's age- and gender-controlled top-100 1to3gram correlations (Schwartz et al. 2013); N weights are negated because WWBP's 'neu' column is oriented towards emotional stability.

Dark Triad weights are the historical package's word-level expansion of word2vec cluster coefficients; intercepts are parsed (not executed) from its index.js. The coefficients are for standardized cluster fractions, so each is divided by its cluster's population SD and weight × mean / SD is subtracted from the intercept, using statistics of the authors' released dataset (data/darktriad-scaling.json; 102 of 104 clusters, the other two keep their weights). Groups under 500 tokens produce a warning, following the authors' recommendation.
Spreadsheet artefacts that the Happier Fun Tokenizer cannot produce are removed: PERMA #NAME?, #REF! and Err:508; Big Five '93.00%' and '0.93%'.
PERMA 'TRUE' (spreadsheet boolean conversion) is restored to 'true'.
Big Five double quotes lost in conversion are restored: '' to '"', ' -' to '" -', ': ' to ': "'; 'the lord,' becomes the HFT trigram 'the lord ,'.
UTF-8 terms mis-decoded as cp1252 are repaired, e.g. 'â™¥' to '♥' and 'don â€™ t' to 'don ’ t' (age, gender, PERMA).
Doubled backslashes in affect, age and gender terms, e.g. ':\\', are restored to the single-backslash HFT tokens they escape.

Affect, PERMA and Spanish PERMA use binary per-message encoding, and a group's score is the mean of its message scores (Schwartz et al. 2016; Smith et al. 2016; affect inferred, see docs/research.md).
Temporal orientation uses binary per-message encoding; a group's score is the proportion of messages classified as each class (Schwartz et al. 2015; Park et al. 2016).
Default ngram sizes are the token counts of the vocabulary under HFT, where spaced dots ('. . .') are one token; age and gender are therefore unigram-only, as in Sap et al. (2014).
The tokenizer is a port of the pinned DLATK Happier Fun Tokenizer; scripts/dlatk-reference.py executes that file only to regenerate test fixtures.
Optimism is not a lexicon: following WWBP's guidance, messages classified as future-oriented by the temporal orientation lexicon are scored with the affect lexicon.
